issues.body: `_worker_no_change_pred` returns false when `worker_no_change_rate_1h` is null, and `compute_recoveries` still adds a recovery whenever that predicate is false for every row in the recovery window. Thus, after `recover_snapshots` consecutive unreadable-ledger snapshots, a collected target can auto-close an existing `worker-no-change` alert without any measured evidence that the rate cleared. The collection-target guard does not prevent this because worker-run collection can succeed while only the auxiliary health ledger is unavailable. The new test proves recovery for measured 0.0 snapshots, but it never starts from null-rate snapshots and therefore does not catch this path.
issues.fix_hint: Give this class a measurable-clear recovery condition: require each recovery-window row to have a numeric no-change rate (and the required sample semantics) before declaring `WORKER_NO_CHANGE` recovered. Add a non-vacuous assertion that two collected null-rate snapshots do not include `(target, WORKER_NO_CHANGE)` in recoveries, while two measured healthy snapshots still do.
issues.title: Unavailable no-change telemetry is still treated as confirmed recovery

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 major finding remains unchanged. Missing model-health evidence correctly suppresses firing, but the generic recovery rule still treats a false predicate as proof of clearance. Consequently, consecutive snapshots with a null no-change rate can auto-close a live worker-no-change alert. The added recovery test covers measured healthy snapshots only and does not exercise the unavailable-telemetry case. Progress is stagnant because the same fail-open recovery path remains at the same severity.
